papers.title_in_file: Quantum Convolutional Neural Networks are Effectively Classically Simulable
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results, discussion and conclusion read from pdftotext output.
papers.what_it_is: A paper arguing that tracing-out and measurement-based QCNNs are classically simulable on standard benchmarks, with a trained classical surrogate.

assertions.value: The authors report constructing and training a purely classical QCNN surrogate, based on low-bodyness Pauli propagation, tensor networks and classical shadows, that matches or outperforms standard QCNNs on all benchmark datasets, on up to 1024 qubits.
quotes: purely classical QCNN surrogate--based on low-bodyness Pauli propagation, tensor networks, and
classical shadows--that matches or outperforms standard QCNNs on all benchmark datasets and
on up-to 1024 qubits, thereby empirically realizing our simulability claims.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on the benchmark datasets the authors chose.
assertions.reader_inference: The surrogate result holds for the benchmarked, locally-easy datasets only; it does not show every QML model is simulable.

assertions.value: The authors state that their work does not intend to prove that no scenario needs a QCNN trained on a quantum computer, that the burden of proof now rests on proponents of QCNNs, and that their claims do not amount to a full dequantization of QCNNs.
quotes: Clearly, our work cannot, and does not intend to, prove
the burden of proof now rests firmly in the hands of any
amount to a full dequantization of QCNNs.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of the scope and limits of its claim.

assertions.value: The authors state that there is currently no evidence that QCNNs will work on classically non-trivial tasks, and that their exhaustive literature search did not produce a single example of a task that cannot be classified by simulating the QCNN in the low-bodyness subspace.

assertions.reader_inference: An absence claim: it depends on the completeness of the literature search.

assertions.value: The authors propose a new nonlinear activation function for the quantum neuron that is not periodic, so it can take any real numbers, and whose neurons can be trained with efficient gradient descent.
quotes: propose a new nonlinear activation function that is not periodic so it can take
any real numbers and its neurons can be trained with efficient gradient descent.

assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on very small datasets.

assertions.value: The paper proves that a QBM learning solution can be obtained with stochastic gradient descent using at most a polynomial number of Gibbs states.
quotes: plateaus. We prove that a solution can be obtained with stochastic gradient descent using at most a
polynomial number of Gibbs states.
assertions.certainty_reason: A proof stated by the authors.

assertions.value: The paper proves that pre-training on a subset of the QBM parameters can only lower the sample complexity bounds.

eters can only lower the sample complexity bounds.

assertions.value: The authors state that the bounds make no assumption on the form of the Hamiltonian ansatz other than that it consists of polynomially many terms, and apply to all types of QBMs without hidden units.

papers.title_in_file: Overcoming the Coherence Time Barrier in Quantum Machine Learning on Temporal Data
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results, discussion and conclusion read from pdftotext output.
papers.what_it_is: A paper presenting NISQRC, a quantum reservoir computing algorithm using mid-circuit measurement and reset for inference on temporal data, tested in simulation and on IBM hardware.

assertions.value: The authors present NISQRC for qubit-based quantum systems, which enables inference on temporal data over durations unconstrained by decoherence, and report demonstrating through simulations and experiments on a 7-qubit quantum processor that it can recover arbitrarily long test signals, not limited by coherence time.
quotes: NISQRC, for qubit-based quantum systems that enables inference on temporal data over durations unconstrained
Through simulations and experiments on a 7-qubit quantum processor we demonstrate
that NISQRC can recover arbitrarily long test signals, not limited by coherence time.
